#| tags: [parameters]

# label, n_total, n_train, n_test, dropped (ADATA_TRAINSPLIT)
LABEL_COUNTS = "label_counts.tsv"
# <method>_metrics.tsv, <method>_per_label.tsv and <method>_confusion.tsv (MODEL_EVALUATE);
# missing or empty without the evaluation (--train_evaluate false)
EVALUATION_DIR = "evaluation"
MODEL_NAME = "reference"
VERSIONS_FILE = "versions.yml"
# Confusion matrices with more true labels show the labels with the most test cells
MAX_CONFUSION_LABELS = 50

```{python}
model_name = str(MODEL_NAME)
evaluation_dir = str(EVALUATION_DIR)
max_confusion_labels = int(MAX_CONFUSION_LABELS)

# Category of unlabelled cells (ADATA_TRAINSPLIT)
unknown_category = 'unknown'
method_titles = {'celltypist': 'CellTypist', 'scanvi': 'scANVI'}


def method_title(method: str) -> str:
    return method_titles.get(method, method)


def inline_table_html(df: pd.DataFrame, index: bool = False) -> str:
    """
    A table on a single line, for printing from an `output: asis` cell: pandoc reads the
    indentation of to_html's rows as an indented code block, so every line is stripped.
    """
    return ''.join(line.strip() for line in df.to_html(index=index, na_rep='').splitlines())


def scroll_table_html(df: pd.DataFrame, index: bool = False, max_height: int = 400) -> str:
    return (f"<div style='overflow-y: scroll; overflow-x: auto; max-height: {max_height}px'>"
            f"{inline_table_html(df, index=index)}</div>")


def read_tsv(path: str, **kwargs) -> pd.DataFrame:
    # keep_default_na=False: a label such as "NA" stays a label
    return pd.read_csv(path, sep='\t', keep_default_na=False, na_values=[''], **kwargs)


label_counts = read_tsv(LABEL_COUNTS, dtype={'label': str})
label_counts['dropped'] = label_counts['dropped'].astype(str).str.lower() == 'true'

methods = []
if os.path.isdir(evaluation_dir):
    methods = sorted(name[: -len('_metrics.tsv')] for name in os.listdir(evaluation_dir)
                     if name.endswith('_metrics.tsv'))
```

```{python}
#| output: asis

is_unknown = label_counts['label'] == unknown_category
kept = label_counts[~label_counts['dropped'] & ~is_unknown]
dropped = label_counts[label_counts['dropped']]
n_unknown = int(label_counts.loc[is_unknown, 'n_total'].sum())

print(
    f"\n<p>This report describes the training of the reference model <b>{escape_html(model_name)}</b>: "
    f"{len(kept)} labels with {int(kept['n_total'].sum())} cells were used, "
    f"{len(dropped)} labels with too few cells were dropped, and {n_unknown} cells were unlabelled. "
    f"{'The models were evaluated with ' + ', '.join(method_title(m) for m in methods) + '.' if methods else 'No evaluation was run.'}"
    "</p>\n"
)
```

## <font color='green'>Labels</font>

The labels are used exactly as given in the label column (`--train_label_col`). Only the unknown label (`--train_unknown_label`) and missing values are treated as unlabelled (`unknown`). Labels with fewer cells than `--train_min_cells_per_label` are removed with their cells, from both the evaluation and the final model, so the final model knows no label the evaluation did not test.

```{python}
#| output: asis

# --train_max_cells_per_label: the cells used after the cap, shown only when the cap removed cells
used = label_counts[~label_counts['dropped']]
capped = ({'n_train_used', 'n_all_used'} <= set(label_counts.columns)
          and ((used['n_train_used'] != used['n_train']).any() or (used['n_all_used'] != used['n_total']).any()))

count_columns = ['label', 'n_total', 'n_train', 'n_test'] + (['n_train_used', 'n_all_used'] if capped else [])
counts_table = kept[count_columns].rename(columns={
    'n_total': 'cells', 'n_train': 'training cells', 'n_test': 'test cells',
    'n_train_used': 'training cells used', 'n_all_used': 'cells used for the final model'})
print(f"\n<p>Labels used for training ({len(kept)}):</p>\n")
if capped:
    # A capped label keeps exactly the cap, every other label fewer cells
    max_cells_used = int(used[['n_train_used', 'n_all_used']].to_numpy().max())
    print(f"\n<p><b>Training data downsampled to at most {max_cells_used} cells per label</b> "
          "(<code>--train_max_cells_per_label</code>; the unlabelled cells count as one label). "
          "The test cells are not downsampled.</p>\n")
print(f"\n{scroll_table_html(counts_table)}\n")

if n_unknown:
    unknown_used = ''
    if capped:
        unknown_row = label_counts[is_unknown].iloc[0]
        unknown_used = (f" After downsampling, {int(unknown_row['n_train_used'])} of them are used for the "
                        f"evaluated models and {int(unknown_row['n_all_used'])} for the final model.")
    print(f"\n<p>{n_unknown} unlabelled cells are never tested. CellTypist ignores them; scANVI uses them "
          f"as unlabelled cells in its semi-supervised training.{unknown_used}</p>\n")

if dropped.empty:
    print("\n<p>No label was dropped.</p>\n")
else:
    dropped_table = dropped[['label', 'n_total']].rename(columns={'n_total': 'cells'})
    print(f"\n<details><summary><font color='green'>{len(dropped)} dropped labels</font>"
          f" - click to expand table</summary>{scroll_table_html(dropped_table)}</details>\n")
```

## <font color='green'>Evaluation</font>

**What the test set means.** A share of the labelled cells of every label (`--train_test_fraction`) is held out as a test set, models are trained on the remaining cells with the same settings as the final models, and the held-out cells are predicted with their labels hidden (scANVI maps them as a query onto the reference trained on the training split). By default cells are held out one by one: test cells then come from the same samples as the training cells, so the metrics are optimistic for data from new donors or studies. With `--train_test_split_by <column>` (e.g. a donor column) whole groups are held out instead, which is closer to using the model on new data; labels whose groups all ended up in training have no test cells and are not evaluated.

The final models are trained on all cells (unless `--train_final_on_all false`). The test metrics therefore describe the training *procedure*; they are slightly pessimistic for the final model, which sees more data.

Macro F1 and balanced accuracy weigh every label equally; accuracy and weighted F1 are dominated by the large labels. All averages run over the labels of the test set, so a prediction of a label that has no test cells counts as an error but adds no label of its own.

```{python}
#| output: asis

def metrics_table(method: str) -> pd.Series:
    metrics = read_tsv(os.path.join(evaluation_dir, f'{method}_metrics.tsv'))
    return metrics.set_index('metric')['value']


if not methods:
    print("\n<p>No evaluation results: the evaluation was switched off (<code>--train_evaluate false</code>) "
          "or no method was evaluated.</p>\n")
else:
    comparison = pd.DataFrame({method_title(m): metrics_table(m) for m in methods})
    comparison = comparison.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors='coerce')
    formatted = comparison.copy().astype(object)
    for metric in formatted.index:
        if metric == 'n_cells':
            formatted.loc[metric] = comparison.loc[metric].map(lambda v: '' if pd.isna(v) else f'{int(v)}')
        else:
            formatted.loc[metric] = comparison.loc[metric].map(lambda v: '' if pd.isna(v) else f'{v:.3f}')
    print("\n<p>Overall metrics on the test cells:</p>\n")
    print(f"\n{inline_table_html(formatted.rename_axis('metric').reset_index())}\n")
```

```{python}
def confusion_png(confusion: pd.DataFrame, title: str) -> tuple:
    """
    Heatmap of the confusion matrix normalised per true label (each row sums to 1).

    With more than max_confusion_labels true labels, the rows show the labels with the most
    test cells; columns follow the rows, then other predicted labels while there is room, and
    the rest are summed into one 'other' column. Returns (base64 PNG, note or None).
    """
    fractions = confusion.div(confusion.sum(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan), axis=0).fillna(0)
    note = None

    rows = list(confusion.index)
    if len(rows) > max_confusion_labels:
        support = confusion.sum(axis=1)
        top = set(support.sort_values(ascending=False).index[:max_confusion_labels])
        rows = [label for label in confusion.index if label in top]
        note = (f"Showing the {len(rows)} true labels with the most test cells out of "
                f"{len(confusion.index)}.")

    extra = [label for label in confusion.columns if label not in rows
             and fractions.loc[rows, label].sum() > 0]
    room = max(0, max_confusion_labels - len(rows))
    columns = rows + extra[:room]
    other = [label for label in confusion.columns if label not in columns]

    shown = fractions.loc[rows, columns].copy()
    if other and fractions.loc[rows, other].to_numpy().sum() > 0:
        shown[f'other ({len(other)} labels)'] = fractions.loc[rows, other].sum(axis=1)

    n_rows, n_cols = shown.shape
    fig_width = min(max(5, 0.3 * n_cols + 3), 22)
    fig_height = min(max(4, 0.3 * n_rows + 2), 22)
    font_size = 8 if max(n_rows, n_cols) <= 30 else 6

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(fig_width, fig_height))
    image = ax.imshow(shown.to_numpy(), cmap='Blues', vmin=0, vmax=1, aspect='auto')
    ax.set_xticks(range(n_cols))
    ax.set_xticklabels(shown.columns, rotation=90, fontsize=font_size)
    ax.set_yticks(range(n_rows))
    ax.set_yticklabels(shown.index, fontsize=font_size)
    ax.set_xlabel('predicted label')
    ax.set_ylabel('true label')
    ax.set_title(title)

    # Percentages in the cells only while they stay readable
    if n_rows <= 25 and n_cols <= 25:
        for i in range(n_rows):
            for j in range(n_cols):
                value = shown.iat[i, j]
                if value >= 0.005:
                    ax.text(j, i, f'{100 * value:.0f}', ha='center', va='center', fontsize=6,
                            color='white' if value > 0.5 else 'black')

    fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, fraction=0.03, pad=0.02, label='fraction of the true label')
    fig.tight_layout()

    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buffer, format='png', dpi=120, bbox_inches='tight')
    plt.close(fig)
    return base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode('utf-8'), note
```

```{python}
#| output: asis

for method in methods:
    title = method_title(method)
    print(f"\n### <font color='green'>{escape_html(title)}</font>\n")

    per_label_path = os.path.join(evaluation_dir, f'{method}_per_label.tsv')
    if os.path.exists(per_label_path):
        per_label = read_tsv(per_label_path, dtype={'label': str})
        # Worst labels first; labels that only occur as predictions (no F1) last
        per_label = per_label.sort_values(['f1', 'support'], ascending=[True, False], na_position='last')
        for col in ['precision', 'recall', 'f1']:
            per_label[col] = per_label[col].map(lambda v: '' if pd.isna(v) else f'{v:.3f}')
        per_label = per_label.rename(columns={'support': 'test cells', 'n_predicted': 'predicted cells'})
        print(f"\n<details><summary><font color='green'>Per-label precision, recall and F1, lowest F1 first"
              f"</font> - click to expand table</summary>{scroll_table_html(per_label)}"
              "<p>Empty cells are undefined: the precision of a label that was never predicted, and the "
              "recall and F1 of a predicted label without test cells.</p></details>\n")
    else:
        print(f"\n<p>No per-label table for {escape_html(title)}.</p>\n")

    confusion_path = os.path.join(evaluation_dir, f'{method}_confusion.tsv')
    if os.path.exists(confusion_path):
        confusion = read_tsv(confusion_path, index_col=0, dtype=str)
        confusion.index = confusion.index.astype(str)
        confusion.columns = confusion.columns.astype(str)
        confusion = confusion.apply(pd.to_numeric, errors='coerce').fillna(0)
        image_string, note = confusion_png(confusion, f'{title}: confusion matrix (per true label)')
        caption = ("Rows are the true labels and sum to 1; columns are the predicted labels. "
                   "The diagonal holds the correctly predicted cells.")
        if note:
            caption += ' ' + note
        print(f'\n<figure><img alt="{escape_html(title)} confusion matrix" '
              f'src="data:image/png;base64,{image_string}" />'
              f'<figcaption>{escape_html(caption)}</figcaption></figure>\n')
    else:
        print(f"\n<p>No confusion matrix for {escape_html(title)}.</p>\n")
```

## <font color='green'>Using the models</font>

The models are written to `models/` in the output directory: the CellTypist model to `models/celltypist/<name>.pkl`, the scVI and scANVI models to `models/scvi/<name>/model.pt` and `models/scanvi/<name>/model.pt`, and the reference cells with the scANVI latent space and labels to `models/<name>_reference.h5ad`. To annotate new data in the `qc_clustering` stage, pass `--celltypist_model models/celltypist/<name>.pkl` and/or `--scanvi_model models/scanvi/<name>/model.pt` with `--integration_methods scvi,scanvi`.

## <font color='green'>Software versions</font>

The first table lists the software of the pipeline modules that produced the results in
this report, as collected by Nextflow. The second one is read from the rendering
environment itself, so it describes the software that produced the report.

```{python}
def pipeline_versions(path: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """
    Software versions collected by Nextflow from the modules of this stage.

    The file is the collated versions.yml of the pipeline: one mapping per process, each
    holding the tools that process reported. It is flattened into one row per tool so the
    table reads the same way as the one below.
    """
    import yaml

    collected = {}
    if os.path.exists(path):
        with open(path) as handle:
            collected = yaml.safe_load(handle) or {}

    rows = [
        (process, tool, str(version))
        for process, tools in collected.items()
        for tool, version in (tools or {}).items()
    ]

    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=['process', 'software', 'version'])


modules = pipeline_versions(str(VERSIONS_FILE))

display(HTML('<font color="black">' + modules.to_html(index=False) + '</font>'))
```

```{python}
import platform
import shutil
import subprocess

import IPython


def library_version(module) -> str:
    """
    Version of an already imported library.

    The attribute is preferred over the installed distribution metadata because it is what
    the running code reports about itself; the metadata is only consulted as a fallback.
    """
    reported = getattr(module, '__version__', None)
    if reported:
        return str(reported)

    from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version as distribution_version

    try:
        return distribution_version(module.__name__)
    except PackageNotFoundError:
        return 'unknown'


def quarto_version():
    """
    Version of the quarto binary rendering this document, or None if it cannot be read.

    Quarto does not export its own version into the rendering environment, so the binary is
    asked directly. The row is dropped rather than guessed when no binary can be reached.
    """
    reported = os.environ.get('QUARTO_VERSION')
    if reported and reported.strip():
        return reported.strip()

    bin_path = os.environ.get('QUARTO_BIN_PATH')
    candidates = [os.path.join(bin_path, 'quarto')] if bin_path else []
    candidates.append(shutil.which('quarto'))

    for candidate in candidates:
        if not candidate or not os.path.exists(candidate):
            continue
        try:
            completed = subprocess.run(
                [candidate, '--version'],
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                timeout=60,
                check=True,
            )
        except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
            continue
        if completed.stdout.strip():
            return completed.stdout.strip()

    return None
```
